candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / De Incarnatione Verbi §34
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §34 (c. 350 AD)

'He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief' — Athanasius marks Isa 53:3-5 as the MOST-EXPLICIT prophetic-anchor of the Suffering-Servant theology the Word-incarnate fulfills. The despising-and-rejection are borne by the assumed-humanity (Word-IN-the-flesh tasting human rejection on behalf of all-the-rejected); the bearing-of-griefs (LXX houtos tas hamartias hēmōn pherei) is the substitutionary-atonement-mechanism. The Word's-impassible-divinity is preserved (the Word-qua-Word cannot suffer); the assumed-flesh truly-suffers, and the suffering is salvifically-imputed to the Word's-Person. Pairs with 1 Pet 2:24 (hos tas hamartias hēmōn autos anēnenken en tō sōmati autou epi to xylon) as the canonical Suffering-Servant-fulfilled-in-Christ pair.
